title: Top compact-support cohomology: dimension bound, dense restriction and cover presentation
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a compactifiable separated finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $B$ be a finite commutative ring and $G$ any sheaf of $B$-modules on the ordinary small etale site of $X$. Use $Rf_!$ and its cohomology sheaves $R^qf_!G=\mathcal H^q(Rf_!G)$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Suppose every geometric fibre of $f$ has dimension at most $d\geq0$, where dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then $R^qf_!G=0$ for $q>2d$ and $R^{2d}f_!$ is right exact. For every geometric point $\bar s$ there is a natural identification $(R^qf_!G)_{\bar s}=H_c^q(X_{\bar s},G|_{X_{\bar s}})$, with compact cohomology defined using any proper compactification.

If $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is a quasi-compact open immersion whose closed complement has geometric fibres of dimension strictly less than $d$, extension by zero induces an isomorphism $R^{2d}(fj)_!j^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}R^{2d}f_!G$. If $(u_i:X_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ is a finite jointly surjective family of separated etale morphisms of finite type, put $X_{ij}=X_i\times_X X_j$ and let $u_{ij}:X_{ij}\to X$ be the structural map [def-pc-fibre-product]. The etale sum-extension counits give an exact coequalizer presentation
$$\bigoplus_{i,j}R^{2d}(fu_{ij})_!u_{ij}^*G\rightrightarrows\bigoplus_iR^{2d}(fu_i)_!u_i^*G\longrightarrow R^{2d}f_!G\longrightarrow0.$$
Finally, if $g:W\to X$ is compactifiable separated finite type with geometric fibres of dimension at most $e$, then the canonical composition comparison induces the corner isomorphism $R^{2d}f_!R^{2e}g_!H\xrightarrow{\sim}R^{2(d+e)}(fg)_!H$ for every sheaf $H$ of $B$-modules on $W$. These maps are natural in the sheaves.

source.place: XVII 5.2.8 and Corollary 5.2.8.1 (p. 358), 6.2.9–6.2.10 (pp. 428–430); dense restriction and top corner: SGA4-expose-18_reedition.pdf XVIII Lemmas 2.1–2.2 and 2.7.1–2.7.2 (pp. 550–552). No Stacks tag located for this combined compact-support interface.

proof.text: Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S$. Properness makes $p$ finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $\overline X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is therefore quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; since $X$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $a$ quasi-compact, as required by the base-change theorem in Step 2. Compute $Rf_!=Rp_*Da_!$ as in [def-amb-etale-compact-support], using [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] to identify different choices. Exactness of $a_!$ is [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] makes $Da_!$ triangulated. The module-sheaf categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and $p_*$ is additive left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]; [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] therefore makes $Rp_*$ triangulated on $D^+$. Thus $Rf_!$ is additive, commutes with shifts, and preserves distinguished triangles. For a sheaf $G$, [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative](1) applied to $a_!G[0]$ with $n=0$ gives a complex $I$ of injectives with $I^r=0$ for $r<0$ representing $a_!G[0]$. Its image $p_*I$ also has zero terms in negative degrees, so $Rf_!G$ has no negative cohomology. By part (2) of the same lemma $I$ is K-injective; hence the bounded-below and unbounded interpretations agree because both apply $p_*$ to $I$. All arguments below use only $D^+$.

Let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Put $U=X_{\bar s}$, $T=\overline X_{\bar s}$ and $a_{\bar s}:U\hookrightarrow T$. Base change is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Apply [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] to the sheaf $G[0]$ and this geometric base change: $\bar s^*Rf_!G\cong R(U/\Omega)_!G_{\bar s}$, computed on the pulled-back compactification. The inverse image on constant-$B$ modules is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so it commutes with cohomology. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], sections on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ are exact and identify sections of $\bar s^*F$ with $F_{\bar s}$ (the identification respects $B$ by naturality with respect to scalar multiplication). The definition of direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] then gives, naturally,
$$(R^qf_!G)_{\bar s}\cong H^q_B(T,a_{\bar s!}G_{\bar s})=:H_c^q(U,G_{\bar s}).$$
For $q\geq0$ its underlying abelian group is $H^q(T,(a_{\bar s!}G_{\bar s})_{\rm ab})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget]; negative degrees vanish by Step 1. Independence from the chosen compactification follows from [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], also applied over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$.

For the dimension bound fix the geometric point of Step 2. $T$ is proper, hence finite type over $\Omega$ by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field has only the ideals zero and the unit ideal. Let $C\hookrightarrow T$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|U|}$, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is proper over $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], hence finite type and Noetherian. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] its underlying space has finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_r$. Give each its reduced induced closed structure in $T$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; each is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme] and proper, hence finite type over $\Omega$. This uses only the underlying closed support, and does not assert that the possibly nonreduced scheme $U$ factors through $C$.

source.place: XVII Corollary 5.2.8.1, proof: proper closure of the geometric fibre

proof.text: Each component $C_i$ meets $U$: otherwise the union of the other finitely many components, a closed subset, would contain $U$, hence its closure $|C|$, contradicting maximality of $C_i$. The open subset $V_i=C_i\cap U$ in the integral finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $C_i$ is nonempty, so [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] gives $\dim C_i=\dim V_i$. Since $V_i$ is closed in $U$, each strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $V_i$ is such a chain in $U$; hence $\dim C_i\leq\dim U\leq d$. Every finite chain of irreducible closed subsets of $C$ lies in one $C_i$: its largest member is irreducible and the finitely many closed $C_i$ cover it. Thus $\dim C\leq d$, directly from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. This bounds the closure of the original fibre inside the compactified fibre, rather than bounding all of $T$.

source.place: XVII Corollary 5.2.8.1, proof: equality of the dimension of a dense open over a field

proof.text: Write $E=(a_{\bar s!}G_{\bar s})_{\rm ab}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], $E$ is zero outside $U$, hence outside $C$. If $C$ is empty then $E=0$ by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], and its cohomology is zero using the zero resolution [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Otherwise [lem-kun-04ca] gives $E\cong i_*L$ for the closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow T$, with $L=i^{-1}E$. If $N\geq1$ is the additive exponent of the finite ring $B$, then $N\cdot m=(N\cdot1_B)m=0$ for every $B$-module element. Thus $NE=0$, and exact additive inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] gives $NL=0$. In particular $L$ is a torsion abelian sheaf, with no finite-stalk or constructibility condition. The immersion $i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] gives $H^q(T,E)\cong H^q(C,L)$ for every $q\geq0$.

source.place: XVII Corollary 5.2.8.1, proof: reduce to torsion cohomology on a proper support

proof.text: The algebraically closed field $\Omega$ is separably closed, so [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(\Omega)\leq0$. By [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] the finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $C$ has torsion cohomological dimension at most $2\dim C\leq2d$. The definition [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] therefore gives $H^q(C,L)=0$ for $q>2d$. Steps 2 and 5 identify this with the underlying abelian group of $(R^qf_!G)_{\bar s}$. This holds at every geometric point, so [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to $0\to R^qf_!G$ after forgetting coefficients, proves $R^qf_!G=0$. The coefficient-forgetting functor is exact and faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], so zero underlying sheaf means zero module sheaf. No assumption of invertibility of $N$ is used.

source.place: XVII Corollary 5.2.8.1, proof using SGA4 X 4.3

proof.text:
Put $n=2d$. For a short exact sequence $0\to G'\to G\to G''\to0$ of $B$-module sheaves, the cone of $G'[0]\to G[0]$ maps quasi-isomorphically to $G''[0]$: its only possible cohomology is the kernel in degree $-1$ (zero) and the cokernel in degree zero ($G''$). Thus [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes it a distinguished triangle. Step 1 and [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] give
$$R^nf_!G'\longrightarrow R^nf_!G\longrightarrow R^nf_!G''\longrightarrow R^{n+1}f_!G'=0.$$
This proves preservation of epimorphisms. For any right exact sequence $A\to B'\to C'\to0$, let $I$ be the image of $A\to B'$. Apply the displayed assertion to $0\to I\to B'\to C'\to0$, and preservation of epimorphisms to $A\to I$; the image of $R^nf_!A\to R^nf_!B'$ is consequently the kernel of $R^nf_!B'\to R^nf_!C'$. This is right exactness of $R^nf_!$.

For the open immersion in the statement let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced induced closed complement, provided by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The closed complement is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since its closed immersion is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a). Noetherian schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compact-support-open-closed-triangle] applies and gives the exact segment
$$R^{2d-1}(fi)_!i^*G\longrightarrow R^{2d}(fj)_!j^*G\longrightarrow R^{2d}f_!G\longrightarrow R^{2d}(fi)_!i^*G.$$
The needed compactifications exist by [thm-nagata-compactification]; $fi$ is separated finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite, lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-separated-finite-type]. The composite $fj$ is locally finite type and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type, lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (an open immersion has closed diagonal because its self-fibre-product is itself). Its source is a quasi-compact open of a Noetherian scheme and hence quasi-compact; its target $S$ is quasi-separated, so it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], and therefore finite type. For $d\geq1$ the geometric fibres of $fi$ have dimension at most $d-1$, so Step 6 applied with $d-1$ kills both outer terms. For $d=0$, a space of dimension strictly less than zero has no points (a point has a nonempty irreducible closure and hence a chain of length zero); every geometric fibre of $Z$ is empty, and Step 2 gives zero outer terms (degree $-1$ also vanishes by Step 1). Exactness gives the required isomorphism, induced by extension by zero. The reduction of the closed complement changes none of its topological dimensions.

For the finite etale cover define sheaves on $X$
$$C_0=\bigoplus_i u_{i,\Sigma!}u_i^*G,\qquad C_1=\bigoplus_{i,j}u_{ij,\Sigma!}u_{ij}^*G.$$
The two maps are the sum-extension counits along the projections $X_{ij}\to X_i,X_j$, and $C_0\to G$ is the sum of the counits. These are the adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], for the functors [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ and let $J$ be the set of lifts of $\bar x$ to the disjoint union of the $X_i$. Joint surjectivity makes $J$ nonempty: choose a point of some $X_i$ over the image $x$ of $\bar x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] its residue field is a finite separable extension of $\kappa(x)$, which embeds in the algebraically closed $\Omega$ over the given embedding of $\kappa(x)$; this produces a lift. The projections $X_{ij}\to X_i$ and $X_{ij}\to X_j$ are etale: they are base changes of $u_j$ and $u_i$, respectively, by part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Part (2), taking the fibre product over the final object $X/X$, says that the structural map $u_{ij}$ is etale as well. By [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks], [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], and [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits], the underlying stalk complex is
$$\bigoplus_{(a,b)\in J^2}M\xrightarrow{[a,b,m]\mapsto[a,m]-[b,m]}\bigoplus_{a\in J}M\xrightarrow{\sum}M\to0,\qquad M=G_{\bar x}.$$
The stalk identifications preserve the $B$-action since all germ maps do. The counit evaluates each lift summand, so the displayed maps have exactly these formulas. Choose $a_0\in J$. The sum map is onto by $m\mapsto[a_0,m]$, and a finite tuple $\sum_a[a,m_a]$ with $\sum m_a=0$ equals $\sum_a([a,m_a]-[a_0,m_a])$, hence lies in the image of the first map. This proves stalk exactness, including when $M=0$. Exact stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] imply $C_1\to C_0\to G\to0$ is exact (apply them to its homology objects); exactness of forgetting module structure is [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. The joint-surjectivity hypothesis is essential: the printed XVIII 2.2 omits it explicitly, but its proof cites XVII 6.2.9, which assumes it. For the identity of a geometric point, a family consisting only of the empty scheme would give a zero augmentation to a nonzero sheaf.

Apply the right exact additive functor $R^{2d}f_!$ of Step 7 to $C_1\to C_0\to G\to0$. Finite direct sums are biproducts, so additivity identifies their images with the corresponding finite sums (the inclusion/projection identities are preserved). By [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization], compactified $Ru_{i!}$ and $Ru_{ij!}$ are the exact degreewise sum-extension functors, including their specified counits. By [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] their composition with $Rf_!$ is canonically $R(fu_i)_!$ and $R(fu_{ij})_!$. For precision, $X_{ij}\to X_i$ is separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. The maps $X_i\to X$ are finite type by hypothesis, so $X_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; applying that lemma to $X_{ij}\to X_i$ then shows that $X_{ij}$ is Noetherian. Separatedness and local finite type of $u_{ij}$ and of all composites with $f$ follow from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Their Noetherian sources are quasi-compact by the definition of Noetherianity, and their Noetherian targets are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) supplies quasi-compactness, hence finite type. Their compactifications exist by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Thus every application of the compact-support normalization and composition has the required hypotheses. We obtain precisely the displayed pair of arrows and the augmentation in the item. In an additive category, the cokernel of the difference of two arrows is their coequalizer, since a map annihilates the difference exactly when it equalizes the arrows. This proves the asserted presentation.

We make the top-corner argument without assuming that compact support is the right derived functor of its degree-zero part. For $K$ with cohomology in a finite interval $[a,b]$, prove $\mathcal H^r(Rf_!K)=0$ for $r>2d+b$ by induction on $b-a+1$. If there is no cohomology, $K\cong0$ because a complex with zero cohomology is quasi-isomorphic to zero [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For one degree, the canonical truncation is quasi-isomorphic to $\mathcal H^a(K)[-a]$, by the explicit good truncations [def-kun-truncations]; Step 6 and the shift compatibility of Step 1 give the bound. For the induction step use the functorial triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]
$$\tau_{\leq b-1}K\to K\to\mathcal H^b(K)[-b]\to(\tau_{\leq b-1}K)[1],$$
where $K\cong\tau_{\leq b}K$. The first term has cohomology in $[a,b-1]$ and its image under $Rf_!$ vanishes above $2d+b-1$ by induction; the last term's image vanishes above $2d+b$ by Step 6 and shifts. Applying Step 1 and the long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives the bound for $K$. The induction uses only the existence and functoriality of the truncation triangles, not uniqueness of their connecting morphisms.

source.place: XVII 5.1.8.1–5.1.8.3; XVIII 2.7, explicit finite truncation proof of the maximum-cycle argument

proof.text:
Apply Steps 1 and 6 to $g$ with the arbitrary sheaf $H$: $K=Rg_!H$ has cohomology only in $[0,2e]$. All schemes here are Noetherian, including $W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Put $Q=\tau_{\leq2e-1}K$ and $N=2(d+e)$. Step 11 gives $\mathcal H^r(Rf_!Q)=0$ for $r>2d+2e-1=N-1$; if $e=0$, then $Q=0$ and the same conclusion holds. Apply $Rf_!$ to the canonical top truncation triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], and take cohomology in degree $N$ using [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. The two adjacent terms $\mathcal H^N(Rf_!Q)$ and $\mathcal H^{N+1}(Rf_!Q)$ vanish, so the canonical map gives an isomorphism
$$\mathcal H^N(Rf_!Rg_!H)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^N(Rf_!\mathcal H^{2e}(Rg_!H)[-2e])=R^{2d}f_!R^{2e}g_!H.$$
Invert it and use the canonical composition isomorphism $Rf_!Rg_!\cong R(fg)_!$ from [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. This is the asserted corner map $R^{2d}f_!R^{2e}g_!H\cong R^{2(d+e)}(fg)_!H$: it is the maximum-degree edge obtained by the top truncation of the inner functor, exactly the corner in XVIII 2.7.2. It does not require a dimension formula for the fibres of $fg$.

All maps just used are functorial in the sheaves: compact-support base change and composition are natural by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion, lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]; the open-complement map is the triangle map of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compact-support-open-closed-triangle]; the cover maps are the adjunction counits identified, including normalization, by [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]; and the top projection is the functorial good truncation of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. Taking cohomology preserves the commutative squares, as do inverses of the isomorphisms (multiply the same squares by their inverses). Thus the stalk identification, dense-open isomorphism, coequalizer presentation and corner isomorphism have precisely the naturality asserted. No coordinate choices or chosen geometric lift from Step 9 enter the resulting maps: that lift was used only to verify exactness of already specified maps.

proof_origin.place: XVII Proposition 5.2.8 and Corollary 5.2.8.1 (p. 358), 6.2.9–6.2.10 (pp. 428–430); SGA4-expose-18_reedition.pdf XVIII Lemmas 2.1–2.2 (p. 550) and §2.7, equations (2.7.1)–(2.7.2) (p. 552). The closed-support dimension argument and finite truncation induction spell out the fibrewise vanishing proof and maximal-degree corner argument.
